reading.objective: Announce a contemporary art exhibition on light and memory and make the title unforgettable.
reading.audience: Gallery-goers and art press who read contemporary posters closely.
reading.feeling: Quiet, luminous, slightly uncanny, like a bright shape that lingers on the eye after it is gone.

concept.idea: An afterimage is a bright shape followed by its complementary ghost, so the poster is one hot disc of light haunted by a cyan echo that fades in rings: memory as decay of light.
decisions: read first: the vermilion disc and its cyan ghost, then the huge title Afterimage
type: Instrument Serif at large scale for the title, with a ghost copy of the word in the complementary colour; Instrument Sans small for details
colour: warm paper ground, near-black ink, vermilion as the light and its complement teal as the ghost, nothing else
composition: disc high and slightly left, ghost drifting down and right toward the title; title anchors the bottom, details in a quiet row beneath a hairline
forms: one solid disc, one multiplied ghost disc, four fading outline rings that show the trace dying away
